messages.front-open: The front matter has no closing `---`, so Oversay reads it as part of the note.
messages.front-line: `{text}` isn’t a `key: value` line, so Oversay ignores it.
messages.front-key: Oversay doesn’t use `{text}`. The keys are {keys}.
messages.front-length: `{text}` isn’t a length Oversay reads. Write it like `30m` or `1:30:00`.
messages.made-with: `{text}` should be `Oversay skill` and a version, like `Oversay skill 0.2.0`.
messages.deck-value: `{text}` isn’t one Oversay reads, so it uses the default. Write one of {values}.
messages.no-topics: There are no `## Topic` lines, so Oversay shows nothing.
messages.before-topic: This point comes before the first `## Topic` line, so it shows under a topic with no name.
messages.topic-time: Oversay doesn’t read `[{text}]` as a time or a kind, so it shows as part of the topic’s name. Times look like `[10m]`, `[1:30]`, `[~5m]` or `[open]`; the kinds are {kinds}.
messages.heading: `{text}` isn’t shown. Use `## Topic` for a topic, or `- point` for a point.
messages.deep-point: This is deeper than a sub-point, so Oversay shows it as a sub-point. Notes have one level of sub-points.
